name: The Lorca Memorial Olive of Alfacar

location.address: Parque Federico Garcia Lorca, Alfacar, Granada

pin_evidence: Register coordinate only. Sheet: the olive stands beside the monolith, at the end of the park opposite the main gate. No photo or GPS observation of the olive found; Commons CC0 files within 80 m (JakobHosp) show only views and other trees (I looked at two), not the olive.

official_register.name: Arboles y arboledas singulares de Andalucia (REDIAM)

access: Free. Municipal park on the Carretera de la Vega in Alfacar, open all day.
transport: Alfacar is a few km north-east of Granada; bus line 33 links the two (check current timetables), or go by car.
alive_evidence: No dated evidence of the olive itself. The monolith beside it is still the site of annual wreath-layings (Diario Libre 2011; a July 2026 search result about the 80th anniversary was not opened).
facts: Sheet: total height 5.5 m, trunk 2.5 m to the crown, girth 1.50 m at 1.30 m and 1.85 m at the base, crown 4.5 by 4.0 m. A small, young-looking olive: its interest is cultural, not size or age. Source: sheet PDF.

Sheet: listed for cultural-historical reference. It says the poet seems to have been shot in these parts, between Alfacar and Viznar, and that a monolith was raised beside the olive in honour of him and of those shot there ('parece ser', the sheet is hedged). Source: sheet PDF.
Sheet: single stem with a high fork and a spherical crown; people leave papers with poems in the hollows of the trunk in memory of the poet. Source: sheet PDF.
Sheet, setting: on the outskirts of Alfacar in a park dedicated to Garcia Lorca, a varied ornamental garden ringed by Aleppo pine, at the far end from the main entrance. Source: sheet PDF.
Diario Libre (17 Aug 2011): a floral offering was laid at the monolith 'beside the olive where he died shot'. Source: Diario Libre URL.

Search results (not opened) say the route between Viznar and Alfacar was inaugurated in 1986 by the Diputacion de Granada and another source says the park dates from 1992; sources disagree, do not state either.
verify_notes: Two sources for existence and the olive-beside-monolith (sheet, Diario Libre); access from Spainseeker. Whether Lorca was shot at THIS olive is a claim the sheet hedges and the Diario piece states flatly; the site of his death and remains is disputed (a search result says the idea his remains lay in this park is now discounted). Writer must keep it as 'the memorial olive' and attribute the claim, never assert. The tree is not old by size (1.5 m girth); it ships for cultural reason, on a judgement for Hidde. No photograph, pin approximate (park is not a small site). Not a living person's name issue: historical figure.
story:
People leave papers with poems in the hollows of this olive's trunk, in memory of Federico Garcia Lorca. It is not an old tree, or a big one. The Junta de Andalucia's register measures 5.5 metres of height and 1.50 metres of girth, a young-looking olive with a high fork and a round crown, and lists it for cultural and historical reasons alone.

What matters is what stands beside it. The register says the poet seems to have been shot in these parts, between Alfacar and Viznar, and that a monolith was raised beside this olive in his honour and in honour of the others shot here. A 2011 newspaper report of the wreath-laying at the monolith went further and called it the olive where he died. Neither claim is settled. Where Lorca was killed and where his remains lie are still disputed, and one account says the idea that he lies in this park is now discounted. So this page calls it what it can stand behind, the memorial olive.

It grows in the Parque Federico Garcia Lorca on the edge of Alfacar, a village a few kilometres north-east of Granada, at the far end of a varied ornamental garden ringed by Aleppo pines, opposite the main gate. The park is free and open all day, and bus line 33 runs from Granada. No photograph of the olive has been published and its pin is the register's point, so look for the monolith and the olive beside it.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the monolith beside it, raised for Lorca and the others shot here; the olive itself is small, 5.5 metres tall. It stands at the far end of the park from the main gate.

name: The Twin-Stemmed Plane of Santo Domingo

location.address: Cacería de Santo Domingo, near the Huetor Vega and Granada boundary

pin_evidence: Register coordinate only. iNaturalist has no tree observation here (two small plant records 75 m and 205 m away). No photograph found.

official_register.name: Arboles y arboledas singulares de Andalucia (REDIAM)

access: Public land (per the register) at a crossing of farm tracks; no trail description found, so treat the way in as unconfirmed.
transport: At the Huetor Vega and Granada boundary, a few km from the city centre; no bus data, best by car or on foot from Huetor Vega.
facts: Sheet: total height 28.5 m, girth at the base 12.70 m on an enormous buttressed base from which two stems rise, fused by the years; stem girths 3.10 m and 5.50 m at 1.30 m. Source: sheet PDF.
Sheet: crown 25.6 by 29.1 m (projection 585.09 sq m). Source: sheet PDF.
Sheet: traces remain of a ladder once used to climb between the two arms, which rise to nearly 29 m. Source: sheet PDF.
Sheet, setting: at a crossing of tracks in open farmland of olive and scattered holm oak on level clay soil, close to the Huetor Vega and Granada boundary. Source: sheet PDF.
verify_notes: Register only, single source, nothing dated, no photo, no pin evidence, access not independently described. Delivered flagged so the register data is kept; fails the findable gate until a photograph or confirmed pin exists. The 12.70 m figure is the girth at the base of the joined stool, not at breast height.
story:
At its foot this plane measures 12.70 metres round. That is the girth of an enormous buttressed base from which two stems rise, fused by the years, in the words of the Junta de Andalucia's register. Measured separately at chest height the two stems are 3.10 and 5.50 metres round, and together they lift the tree to 28.5 metres, with a crown about 26 by 29 metres that covers some 585 square metres of ground.

The register also notes traces of an old ladder that people once used to get up between the two arms, which rise to nearly 29 metres.

It stands at a crossing of tracks in open farmland at the Caceria de Santo Domingo, among olive groves and scattered holm oaks on level clay, close to where Huetor Vega meets Granada, a few kilometres from the city centre.

The register sheet is the only source for this tree, and nothing dated has been published about it since; there is no photograph, the pin is the register's point, and nobody has described the way in on foot. The sheet says the land is public. If you go, tell us what you find, and if you know how old it is, tell us that too.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the huge buttressed base, 12.70 metres round, carrying two fused stems to 28.5 metres. It stands at a crossing of farm tracks among olive groves at the Caceria de Santo Domingo.
